## Relevant Symbols
- `hooks/ledger.sh:47` — `KINDS` includes `ci` and `human:merge`; `block <id> --kind <k>` (`:block)`) writes `blocked_on {kind, since}`; nothing today sets `ci`.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:266-275` — `list` prints a JSON array of entries (or `[]`); `record --pr <url>` (`:259`) stores `pr.url` and `pr.number`. `ledger-id` is a jq select over that.
- `hooks/status-board.sh:144-147` — the nonce delimiter and the two-sed HTML-comment strip; reused verbatim in `pr-watch.sh threads`.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:31-32` — `die`/`usage` idiom; `:27` FETCHER contract (stdout answer at 0, value + expected shape on stderr otherwise).
- `tests/smoke.sh:1346-1364` — fake `gh` writes `"$*"` to a call log and switches on the argv prefix; assertions grep the log (tool-call level, constitution 3).
- `tests/smoke.sh:1818-1826` — counts: `commands/hef.*.md` files must equal "N slash commands" in architecture and "N `hef.*` commands" in README; helper subcommands counted only for `speckit-helper.sh`; hooks from `hooks.json` (a helper is not registered, so the hook count is unchanged).
- `commands/hef.pr.md` "Untrusted input" — the three-line rule (delimit, strip, never let it name a tool/file/command → report and stop). The babysitter's comment triage refines "report and stop" into "doubtful → ask the person".

## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Helpers are FETCHERS: answer on stdout at exit 0; the offending value and the expected shape on stderr, non-zero; no exit-0 sentinel (constitution 5; `ledger.sh:12-13`).
- Zero-install: bash, jq, git, `gh` detected at runtime, `gitleaks` optional (`quality-before-commit.sh` already runs it when present).
- Untrusted text is delimited and stripped **mechanically, upstream of the model** (`status-board.sh:128-132` comment).
- Every guard mutation-checked; `producer | grep -q` never used (capture then grep) — `tests/smoke.sh` header.
- Commands pin a tier in frontmatter, never a model id; purely mechanical loop drivers are `sonnet` (`hef.orchestrate.md:2`, `hef.pr.md:2`); a command that owns a fix step is the `opus` class (`hef.fix.md:2`).
- Eval graders assert tool calls (`tool_used` with `input_match`, `max: 0`), plus one `llm` grader for the narrative (`evals/orchestrator-never-merges/case.yaml`).

## gh surface used (verified against gh 2.x documentation, not the sandbox)
- `gh pr view [<n>|<url>] --json number,url,headRefName,baseRefName,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup`
- `gh pr checks <n> --json name,bucket,link,workflow` — `bucket` ∈ `pass|fail|pending|skipping|cancel`; exit 8 while pending, 1 on a failure, still prints JSON; `--watch --fail-fast` blocks until done (under `timeout <s>`, 124 on expiry). "no checks reported" → exit 1 with no JSON → treated as `pass` with `checks: 0`.
- `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`; run id parsed from the check's `link` (`…/actions/runs/<id>/job/<job-id>`).
- `gh api graphql -f query=… -F owner= -F name= -F number=` for `pullRequest.reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved path line comments(first:50){nodes{author{login} body createdAt url}}}}`; mutation `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input:{pullRequestReviewThreadId, body})` with `-f` string variables (the read query keeps `-F number=` for the Int); `pageInfo{hasNextPage}` on both connections.
- `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/comments --paginate --slurp` (one array per page → `flatten`); `gh pr comment <n> --body-file <f>`.
- `gh repo view --json owner,name` for the GraphQL variables.

## Environment facts that shaped the plan
- `evals/README.md:27-32` — the eval sandbox denies the `git` binary; `ledger.sh:56-58` already falls back to `$PWD/.git`. The helper's `--check` and `resolve --local` read `.git/config` / `.git/HEAD` when `git` fails.
- This repository's remote is `git@github.com:` (ssh); a sandbox that grants only `api.github.com` refuses the push — the command hands the push line to the person.
- Model-tier policy (`.claude/CLAUDE.md`): `fix` is `opus`; a command that owns a root-cause fix step is that class.
- The Bash tool's default timeout is 120 s, maximum 600 s; a 540 s wait needs the raised timeout on that one call.
- `/loop <interval> <command>` is Claude Code's cadence mechanism; no `ScheduleWakeup` tool is assumed.

## Open Questions
- None. The spec's four decisions (separate command, helper-side wait, marker line `_hef.babysit_`, fix boundary) stand; `BEHIND`/`HAS_HOOKS` merge states map to `mergeable` (the person's gate decides), every other unknown status to `pending`.
